results.question: Why do people save items to a wishlist in the first place?
results.restated: Why do people save items to a wishlist on Indian online fashion platforms (what do they say their purpose for saving is)?
results.answer:
Answer
People say they save to wishlist mainly to defer the decision while they resolve the gap between how an item looks online and in person (C2), price questions (C6), fit & size uncertainty (C1), styling & self-image doubts (C3), and to check external reviews (C4) or wait for an action trigger (C13) — and a smaller share say the intent never existed (C9) or faded after saving (C12). Interpretation: The corpus holds nothing on a finer breakdown of “what this is about,” so this is a partial answer.

Evidence
- Material & digital-physical gap (C2): 241 of 1018 records; 226 distinct authors; 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]].
- Price (C6): 207 of 1018; 189 distinct authors; 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]].
- Fit & size uncertainty (C1): 189 of 1018; 185 distinct authors; 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]].
- Styling & self-image (C3): 154 of 1018; 142 distinct authors; 3 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]].
- Fulfilment (returns/friction) (C7): 140 of 1018; 137 distinct authors; 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]].
- External reviews (C4): 82 of 1018; 80 distinct authors; 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]].
- External validation & social proof (C10): 68 of 1018; 67 distinct authors; 3 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C10]].
- Intent extinguished after saving (C12): 54 of 1018; 49 distinct authors; 3 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]].
- Action trigger (journey stage) (C13): 51 of 1018; 50 distinct authors; 3 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C13]].
- Intent never existed (C9): 21 of 1018; 21 distinct authors; 2 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C9]].

- What fraction of wishlist-saves are “never intended to buy” vs deferred intent (as discussed, not as user behavior): “Never intended” appears in 21 of 1018 records (C9) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C9]]. Multiple deferred-intent reasons appear: C2 (241 of 1018), C1 (189 of 1018), C3 (154 of 1018), C4 (82 of 1018), C10 (68 of 1018), and a timing/trigger component (C13) appears in 51 of 1018 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C10]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C13]].
- Sub-themes present in the corpus: price-watching/affordability (C6), checking reviews (C4), partner/peer check (C10), size uncertainty (C1), fabric/colour confidence (C2), outfit fit with self-image/wardrobe (C3), waiting for the right moment to act (C13), intent fading with time (C12), and collecting with no purchase intent (C9) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C10]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C13]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C9]].

In users' words
- “I was cleaning my wishlist yesterday and realised half the clothes I save are not for anything I actually have planned” [[rec|6102d72a4134c75fd1e23e0da192954f39145fbd]].
- “I used to buy for the "vibe" but after I realised the amount of clothes I have… I buy clothes for real life now” [[rec|f25944642b667c3d03053b6c4fda7dec7fb0c41c]].
- “My Instagram feed is currently 90% sarees… I’ve heard mixed reviews about buying from Instagram” [[rec|992e822486c366b967792807472aa652451ea1e2]].
- “he feels I'm very irresponsible with my finances, splurging too much” [[rec|af130b9c55ede19f66e4ea81d42c4464d7ac0e31]].

Variation
- By source (selected examples where the brief reports it):
  - Intent extinguished after saving (C12): Reddit 42 of 309; YouTube 11 of 573; App Store 1 of 22 [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C12]][[analysis_source_code|youtube|C12]][[analysis_source_code|appstore|C12]].
  - Action trigger (C13): Reddit 40 of 309; YouTube 9 of 573; Play 2 of 114 [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C13]][[analysis_source_code|youtube|C13]][[analysis_source_code|play|C13]].
  - External reviews (C4): YouTube 43 of 573; Reddit 33 of 309; App Store 3 of 22; Play 3 of 114 [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C4]][[analysis_source_code|reddit|C4]][[analysis_source_code|appstore|C4]][[analysis_source_code|play|C4]].
  - Price (C6): Reddit 74 of 309; YouTube 70 of 573; Play 60 of 114; App Store 3 of 22 [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C6]][[analysis_source_code|youtube|C6]][[analysis_source_code|play|C6]][[analysis_source_code|appstore|C6]].
  - Intent never existed (C9): YouTube 15 of 573; Reddit 6 of 309 [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C9]][[analysis_source_code|reddit|C9]].
- Interpretation: The corpus holds nothing on a finer breakdown of what this is about (e.g., short- vs long-term saves, urgent need vs casual) beyond the code-level categories.
- Too thin to report across sources for Comparison & decision load (C5): App Store 1 of 22; YouTube 9 of 573; Reddit 12 of 309 [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C5]][[analysis_source_code|youtube|C5]][[analysis_source_code|reddit|C5]].

Counter-evidence
- Rival barriers are also widely discussed, indicating people save items amid multiple unresolved doubts: the gap between how an item looks online and in person (C2): 241 of 1018; fit & size uncertainty (C1): 189 of 1018; styling & self-image (C3): 154 of 1018; fulfilment (C7): 140 of 1018; external validation & social proof (C10): 68 of 1018 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C10]].
- Co-occurrence shows these reasons often travel together rather than alone: C2 with external reviews (C4): 53 joint records; C13 with styling & self-image (C3): 22 joint; C12 with styling & self-image (C3): 22 joint; C13 with price (C6): 20 joint; C11 with price (C6): 15 joint; C12 with C2: 15 joint [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C4]][[analysis_cooccurrence|C13|C3]][[analysis_cooccurrence|C12|C3]][[analysis_cooccurrence|C13|C6]][[analysis_cooccurrence|C11|C6]][[analysis_cooccurrence|C12|C2]].

Confidence
Medium. The corpus is sizeable (denominator 1018) and spans four labeled sources, but the project notes only three independent source types. Agreement with the human coder is reliable for Price (C6) (kappa 0.645), while several other codes used here are “not measurable” for reliability, and two validation thresholds fail overall [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C6]][[analysis_source_code|youtube|C6]][[analysis_source_code|play|C6]][[analysis_source_code|appstore|C6]][[analysis_gold_agreement|C6]][[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]][[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]].

Limitations
- The corpus measures discussion, not behavior; shares are of what people raised, not funnel rates or conversion outcomes [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]].
- The relevance rubric is narrow and likely under-represents price/value and delivery/trust topics; rankings reflect this conditional view of what counts as “reasons for saving” [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]].
- Silent forgetting of wishlists is under-detected by construction; absence in counts is not evidence of low incidence [[analysis_method_flags|stage_a_underdetection]].
- Only about 36% of relevant material is Myntra-specific; most evidence generalizes to Indian online fashion, not to a single platform [[analysis_method_flags|myntra_specific_share]].
- Segment patterns are derived from the same classifications and should not be read as observed user types [[analysis_method_flags|segments_derived_not_observed]].
- Some codes here have small source-specific Ns (e.g., C5) and below-minimum floors; those are reportable but not rankable [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]].
- Price is prominent but cannot be treated as a mandate for discounting; interpretations should focus on transparency, anchoring, and timing [[analysis_method_flags|no_monetary_incentive]].
- Interpretation: The corpus holds nothing on a finer breakdown (e.g., short- vs long-term saves, urgent vs casual browsing), so sub-segmentation of “why save” beyond the listed codes is not supported.
gate_reasons: the corpus holds nothing on a finer breakdown of what this is about
gate_caveats: whether this holds up across sources: too thin to report for C5
how this differs between kinds of shopper: too thin to report for C5

results.question: What stops people from buying the things they have saved?
results.restated: What are the main reasons people give for not buying items they've saved to a wishlist on Indian online fashion platforms?
results.answer:
Answer
People most often talk about not buying wishlisted fashion because of the material & digital-physical gap (C2), price (C6), fit & size uncertainty (C1), styling & self-image (C3), and fulfilment concerns (C7), with most of this discussion sitting in the consideration stage and ending in deferral rather than exit [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]] [[analysis_stage_outcome|C|defer]] [[analysis_stage_outcome|C|exit]].

Evidence
- Material & digital-physical gap (C2): 241 of 1,018 records; 226 distinct authors; 4 sources; consideration stage; deferral outcome [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]].
- Price (C6): 207 of 1,018 records; 189 distinct authors; 4 sources; consideration stage; exit outcome [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]].
- Fit & size uncertainty (C1): 189 of 1,018 records; 185 distinct authors; 4 sources; consideration stage; deferral outcome [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]].
- Styling & self-image (C3): 154 of 1,018 records; 142 distinct authors; 3 sources; consideration stage; deferral outcome [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]].
- Fulfilment (C7): 140 of 1,018 records; 137 distinct authors; 4 sources; consideration stage; exit outcome [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]].
- Social proof from receivers (C4): 82 of 1,018 records; 80 distinct authors; 4 sources; consideration stage; deferral outcome [[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]].
- Where in the journey this appears: consideration-stage deferrals are 526 of 1,018 and exits 199 of 1,018; earlier-stage deferrals are smaller (A: 107 of 1,018; B: 21 of 1,018), with few exits before consideration (A: 3 of 1,018; B: 8 of 1,018) [[analysis_stage_outcome|C|defer]] [[analysis_stage_outcome|C|exit]] [[analysis_stage_outcome|A|defer]] [[analysis_stage_outcome|B|defer]] [[analysis_stage_outcome|A|exit]] [[analysis_stage_outcome|B|exit]].
- Out-of-scope intent (people no longer want the item after saving): Intent extinguished after saving (C12) appears in 54 of 1,018 records, with exit outcomes [[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]].

In users' words
- Price: “price matters a lot” [[rec|571459beb91d9f3f77037651cac8ff269a6bb485]].
- Material/look uncertainty and returns risk: “I'm skeptical about buying it” [[rec|8c0d0711c1c6335c7098f3425e1764d818b4ca46]].
- Returns/fulfilment trust: “they've return policy.... I don't think so that these instagram stores have that” [[rec|8c0d0711c1c6335c7098f3425e1764d818b4ca46]].
- Fulfilment risk and fraud checks: “some people selling fraud product” [[rec|1f0d7052c8faf33dc348ce41dfbbedc22f452724]].

Variation
- By source, the top barriers appear across channels:
  - C2 appears on YouTube (116 of 573; share 0.202), Reddit (104 of 309; share 0.337), Play (18 of 114; share 0.158), and App Store (3 of 22; share 0.136) [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C2]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C2]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C2]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C2]].
  - C6 appears on YouTube (70 of 573; share 0.122), Reddit (74 of 309; share 0.239), Play (60 of 114; share 0.526), and App Store (3 of 22; share 0.136) [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C6]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C6]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C6]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C6]].
  - C1 appears on YouTube (144 of 573; share 0.251), Reddit (40 of 309; share 0.129), Play (3 of 114; share 0.026), and App Store (2 of 22; share 0.091) [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C1]].
- Journey-stage outcomes: consideration dominates discussion with deferral more common than exit in this stage (526 of 1,018 vs 199 of 1,018), while early-stage deferrals are smaller (A: 107 of 1,018; B: 21 of 1,018) and late-stage exits appear as well (D: 50 of 1,018) [[analysis_stage_outcome|C|defer]] [[analysis_stage_outcome|C|exit]] [[analysis_stage_outcome|A|defer]] [[analysis_stage_outcome|B|defer]] [[analysis_stage_outcome|D|exit]].

Counter-evidence
- Other consideration-stage barriers also account for a notable share of discussion: Styling & self-image (C3) at 154 of 1,018; External validation & social proof (C10) at 68 of 1,018; Intent extinguished after saving (C12) at 54 of 1,018; and Action trigger (C13) at 51 of 1,018; plus early-stage issues like Wishlist entry point buried (A2.1) at 47 of 1,018 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C10]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C13]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|A2.1]].
- Some barriers co-occur, suggesting they are not single causes when discussed together (e.g., C2 with C4; C2 with C7; C1 with C3) [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C4]] [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C7]] [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C3]].

Confidence
- Medium. Price (C6) and fit & size uncertainty (C1) clear the agreement threshold (kappa 0.645 and 0.657), but material & digital-physical gap (C2) is weaker (kappa 0.427), and social/fulfilment codes C4 and C7 are not measurable for reliability; two validation thresholds fail overall and relevance recall is estimated, not measured [[analysis_gold_agreement|C6]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C1]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C2]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C4]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C7]] [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]].

Limitations
- Shares report discussion, not user behavior; there is no funnel or conversion data in this corpus [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]].
- Early-stage forgetting and entry-point issues are likely under-detected because they generate fewer posts, so lower counts at Stage A should not be read as low prevalence in behavior [[analysis_method_flags|stage_a_underdetection]].
- The relevance rubric is narrow and likely under-represents price/value and delivery/trust topics; rankings are conditional on that rubric [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]].
- Only about 36% of the corpus is Myntra-specific; platform-mechanical findings should be read as Indian online fashion generally unless otherwise noted [[analysis_method_flags|myntra_specific_share]].
- Segments are derived from classification rules; any lift of confidence-phase codes into “undecided” is partly definitional [[analysis_method_flags|segments_derived_not_observed]].
- App stores are not independent from each other and carry known review skews; triangulation is across roughly three independent source types, not four [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]].
- Price is flagged as a constrainted lever: its prevalence should not be read as an argument for discounting, but for transparency/anchoring/timing solutions [[analysis_method_flags|no_monetary_incentive]].

Interpretation:
- The corpus does not quantify how often users state “I would have bought if X were fixed” versus general complaints; explicit counterfactual intent is not separately counted in the provided facts, so treat the barrier counts as discussion volume, not as conditional purchase statements.
gate_caveats: an ordering of these barriers: too thin to report for C5
whether this holds up across sources: too thin to report for C5

results.question: What are people still uncertain about at the moment they decide whether to buy?
results.restated: Which specific uncertainties do people still report having at the moment they are deciding whether to buy an item saved to a wishlist (the item-level decision moment)?
results.answer:
Answer
At the item-level decision moment, people most often raise the gap between how an item looks online and in person (C2), price (C6), fit & size uncertainty (C1), and styling & self‑image (C3); social‑proof from receivers (C4) and comparison load (C5) appear but are smaller. These doubts frequently travel together — especially C2 with “what did receivers say” (C4), and styling (C3) with both triggers (C13) and “do I still want this” (C12). [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C5]] [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C4]] [[analysis_cooccurrence|C13|C3]] [[analysis_cooccurrence|C12|C3]]

Evidence
- Material & digital-physical gap (C2): 241 of 1,018 records; share 0.237; 226 authors; 4 sources. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]]
- Price (C6): 207 of 1,018; share 0.203; 189 authors; 4 sources. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]]
- Fit & size uncertainty (C1): 189 of 1,018; share 0.186; 185 authors; 4 sources. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]]
- Styling & self-image (C3): 154 of 1,018; share 0.151; 142 authors; 3 sources. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]]
- External validation from receivers (C4): 82 of 1,018; share 0.081; 80 authors; 4 sources. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]]
- Comparison & decision load (C5): 22 of 1,018; share 0.022; 22 authors; 3 sources. Flagged below minimum n for ranking. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C5]] [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]]

Common co-occurrences (pairs above chance)
- C2 with C4: 53 joint records; lift 2.73. [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C4]]
- C13 with C3: 22 joint; lift 2.852. [[analysis_cooccurrence|C13|C3]]
- C12 with C3: 22 joint; lift 2.693. [[analysis_cooccurrence|C12|C3]]
- C2 with C7: 65 joint; lift 1.961. [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C7]]
- C1 with C10: 37 joint; lift 2.931. [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C10]]
Interpretation: These pairings suggest people often seek receiver reviews when worried about digital‑physical gap; styling doubts co‑occur when a trigger makes the decision salient or when intent fades; and size doubts may prompt checking with others.

Finer-grained themes (where available)
- Inside Fit & size (C1): 
  - “Which size” within/among brands (C1.1): 82 of 189 (share 0.434). [[analysis_subcode|C1|C1.1]]
  - Measurements vs charts uncertainty (C1.2): 49 of 189 (share 0.259). [[analysis_subcode|C1|C1.2]]
  - Body shape/proportions fit (C1.3): 25 of 189 (share 0.132). [[analysis_subcode|C1|C1.3]]
  - Return/exchange dependence for sizing (C1.4): 19 of 189 (share 0.101). [[analysis_subcode|C1|C1.4]]
Interpretation: For other codes (C2, C3, C6, C4, C5), the brief does not provide subcode breakdowns, so only top‑level themes are reportable.

Source variation
- C2 appears across sources, with Reddit showing a higher share (104 of 309; share 0.337) than YouTube (116 of 573; share 0.202), Play (18 of 114; share 0.158), App Store (3 of 22; share 0.136). [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C2]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C2]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C2]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C2]]
- C1 is stronger on YouTube (144 of 573; share 0.251) than Reddit (40 of 309; share 0.129), Play (3 of 114; share 0.026), App Store (2 of 22; share 0.091). [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C1]]
- C3 is higher on Reddit (99 of 309; share 0.32) than YouTube (53 of 573; share 0.092) and Play (2 of 114; share 0.018). [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C3]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C3]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C3]]
- C4 appears on YouTube (43 of 573; share 0.075), Reddit (33 of 309; share 0.107), App Store (3 of 22; share 0.136), and Play (3 of 114; share 0.026). [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C4]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C4]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C4]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C4]]
- C6 is present on Reddit (74 of 309; share 0.239) and YouTube (70 of 573; share 0.122). [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C6]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C6]]
- Too thin to report robustness for C5 across sources. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C5]]

In users' words
- “Omggg I was just now adding things to my cart for the B1G1 sale 😭😭 Thank goddddd I check Reddit before ordering from these new stores.” [[rec|b515b6c496b3bf94f2fba6fd110447c1537ac47c]]
- “And I'm 5'7, should I buy an overcoat?” [[rec|a91133402e1ca1100b362aaf8833b2d3cb8d6c61]]
- “Yea but you can’t really find pants for cheaper, and people have a limited amount of pants, unlike tops, so it still isn’t costly” [[rec|349ae8b0c2942f92601d97c5d24cd2f7228a6d1d]]
- “I like this application because what I see I get that like all about the fiting, size, and colour” [[rec|80626558fdb6e4e764bfac305f54b3e8abff8395]]

Variation
- Material & digital-physical gap (C2) is raised more often on Reddit than other sources, while fit & size (C1) is raised more on YouTube; styling (C3) is concentrated on Reddit. [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C2]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C2]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C3]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C3]]
Interpretation: The brief does not break down these patterns by user segment or brand; platform mix reflects discussion, not shopper incidence. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]] [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]]

Counter-evidence
- Other rival barriers at the same stage are also raised: fulfilment (C7) appears in 140 of 1,018 records (share 0.138); external validation “check with partner” (C10) in 68 of 1,018 (share 0.067); intent extinguished (C12) in 54 of 1,018 (share 0.053); action trigger (C13) in 51 of 1,018 (share 0.05); external validation “check elsewhere” (C14) in 38 of 1,018 (share 0.037). [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C10]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C13]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C14]]
- Some barriers rarely appear alone: C2 co-occurs with C4 in 53 records (lift 2.73); styling (C3) co-occurs with triggers (C13) and extinguished intent (C12). [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C4]] [[analysis_cooccurrence|C13|C3]] [[analysis_cooccurrence|C12|C3]]

Confidence
Medium. Fit & size (C1) and price (C6) are supported by reliable agreement with the human coder (kappa 0.657 and 0.645). Material gap (C2) and styling (C3) have weaker agreement (kappa 0.427 and 0.515), so their exact ordering is provisional; C4 and C5 reliability is not measurable. Two validation thresholds fail at the corpus level. [[analysis_gold_agreement|C1]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C6]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C2]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C3]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C4]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C5]] [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]]

Limitations
- Discussion, not shopper behavior: all shares are of what people chose to talk about, not funnel or conversion rates. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]]
- Narrow relevance: the rubric likely under-represents price/value and delivery/trust topics; rankings are conditional on what the rubric kept. [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]]
- Source independence: Google Play and App Store are not independent; effectively three source types. [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]]
- Platform specificity: only about 36% of the corpus is Myntra-specific; most findings describe Indian online fashion generally. [[analysis_method_flags|myntra_specific_share]]
- Thin themes: comparison & decision load (C5) is below the 30‑record floor for ranking; treat any mention as directional only. [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]]
- Segment lifts are partly circular because segments are derived from these codes. [[analysis_method_flags|segments_derived_not_observed]]
Interpretation: The brief does not provide quantified counterfactuals (e.g., “I would have bought if X were fixed”) or workaround counts, so we cannot estimate how often removing a given uncertainty would convert.

premise.asserts: The question asks about uncertainties at the item-decision moment.

gate_caveats: whether this holds up across sources: too thin to report for C5

results.question: What makes people postpone a purchase rather than abandon it altogether?
results.restated: Which barriers discussed in the corpus are associated with shoppers postponing a saved-item purchase (defer) rather than abandoning it completely (exit)?
results.answer:
Answer
Shoppers most often postpone because of the material & digital-physical gap (C2), fit & size uncertainty (C1), and styling & self-image (C3); they most often abandon because of price (C6) and fulfilment frictions (C7). [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]]

Evidence
- How ‘postpone’ vs ‘abandon’ are represented and how many are in each bucket:
  - Consideration stage (C): Defer n=526 of 1018; Exit n=199 of 1018. [[analysis_stage_outcome|C|defer]] [[analysis_stage_outcome|C|exit]]
  - Earlier and later stages (for context only): Stage A Defer n=107 of 1018; Exit n=3 of 1018. Stage B Defer n=21 of 1018; Exit n=8 of 1018. Stage D Exit n=50 of 1018. Broad/meta Stage Z Defer n=15 of 1018; Exit n=8 of 1018. - Which barriers are raised with Defer vs Exit at the Consideration stage (counts, speakers, sources):

    - Material & digital-physical gap (C2) n=241 of 1018; n_distinct_authors=226; n_sources=4. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]]

results.question: What do people go looking for outside the app before they buy?
results.restated: Which external resources or information do people search for or consult outside the shopping app before they complete a purchase (i.e. what do they go looking for off‑platform)?
results.answer:
Answer
People do say they leave the app to “go check this properly somewhere else” (External validation & social proof (C14)), but the corpus is too coarse to tell where they go or what exactly they look for; it does not hold a finer breakdown of off‑app resources. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C14]]

Evidence
- Explicit mentions of leaving the app: 38 of 1018 records (share 0.037) discuss External validation & social proof (C14). [[analysis_code_prevalence|C14]]
- Related needs that often drive checking: Material & digital-physical gap (C2) appears in 241 of 1018 records (share 0.237); Real‑buyer evidence (C4) appears in 82 of 1018 (share 0.081). [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]]
- Workarounds (evidence of effort to verify): For C14, 25 of 38 records include a workaround (share 0.658). [[analysis_workaround|C14]]

[[analysis_source_code|reddit|C14]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C14]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C14]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C14]]

In users' words
- “there is no customer rating & reviews option?” [[rec|aea48d3f4b52061090c5e983ad2790dd364cab14]]
- “product descriptions and reviews are helpful when deciding what to buy” [[rec|f6ae686daf77f145709f48d4315dc6c4b9773a74]]

- By source: Mentions of leaving the app (C14) appear across Reddit, YouTube, App Store, and Play Store, with shares reported above for each source. [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C14]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C14]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C14]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C14]]
- Interpretation: Whether this pattern holds for Fit & size uncertainty (C1), Price (C6), or Comparison & decision load (C5) is too thin to report across sources, per the brief’s instruction; the corpus was not broken down finely enough to separate these at the source level.

Counter-evidence
- Some users say in‑app information is sufficient, reducing the need to go off‑platform: “product descriptions and reviews are helpful when deciding what to buy”. [[rec|f6ae686daf77f145709f48d4315dc6c4b9773a74]]

Confidence
Medium. C14 appears across three independent source types and has workaround and counterfactual signals, but its reliability is not measurable, C4 is not measurable, and C2 has weak agreement with the human coder. Overall validation thresholds failed for the run. [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C14]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C14]] [[analysis_workaround|C14]] [[analysis_counterfactuals|C14]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C14]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C4]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C2]] [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]] [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]]

- The corpus does not hold a finer breakdown of off‑app resources (e.g., which sites, social platforms, or specific search types); the WHAT is largely unspecified in records. Interpretation.

- Relevance rubric is narrow and may under‑capture price/value and delivery/trust discussions; findings are conditional on that filter. [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]]

results.question: How much does fit and size uncertainty matter compared with price?
results.restated: How much does fit & size uncertainty (C1) matter compared with price/value uncertainty (C6) in explaining why people do not buy items they saved to a wishlist on Indian online fashion platforms?
results.answer:
Answer
Price (C6) is raised slightly more often than fit & size uncertainty (C1) in discussion of why wishlisted items don’t get bought, and C6 carries far more explicit “I would have bought if…” statements and more described workarounds than C1. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]] [[analysis_counterfactuals|C6]] [[analysis_counterfactuals|C1]] [[analysis_workaround|C6]] [[analysis_workaround|C1]]

Evidence
- Share of discussion (counts, distinct authors, sources):
  - Price (C6): 207 of 1018 records; 189 distinct authors; from 4 sources. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]]
  - Fit & size uncertainty (C1): 189 of 1018 records; 185 distinct authors; from 4 sources. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]]
- Co-occurrence (compound reasons):
  - C1 with styling & self-image (C3): 40 joint records; lift 1.399. [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C3]]
  - C1 with external validation & social proof (C10): 37 joint records; lift 2.931. [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C10]]

  - C6 with external validation & social proof (C11): 15 joint records; lift 3.074. [[analysis_cooccurrence|C11|C6]]
- Explicit counterfactual purchase intent:
  - C6: 31 counterfactuals out of 201 coded; share 0.154. [[analysis_counterfactuals|C6]]
  - C1: 5 counterfactuals out of 177 coded; share 0.028. [[analysis_counterfactuals|C1]]
- Workarounds and their effort:
  - C6: 30 of 201 coded with workarounds; share 0.149; mean effort 1.6. [[analysis_workaround|C6]]
  - C1: 17 of 177 coded with workarounds; share 0.096; mean effort 1.412. [[analysis_workaround|C1]]
- Source distribution:
  - C6 by source: Reddit 74/309 (share 0.239); YouTube 70/573 (0.122); Play Store 60/114 (0.526); App Store 3/22 (0.136). [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C6]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C6]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C6]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C6]]
  - C1 by source: YouTube 144/573 (0.251); Reddit 40/309 (0.129); Play Store 3/114 (0.026); App Store 2/22 (0.091). [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C1]]
- Overall evidence strength (for orientation):
  - C6 composite 0.707; prevalence 0.203; counterfactual rate 0.15; workaround rate 0.145; mean confidence 0.752. [[analysis_evidence_strength|C6]]
  - C1 composite 0.69; prevalence 0.186; counterfactual rate 0.026; workaround rate 0.09; mean confidence 0.816. [[analysis_evidence_strength|C1]]

In users' words
- “Great Service but Price Are Slightly Higher than other platforms” [[rec|83f902cade59dd75d0914095fcae5638b5ab90ae]]
- “no i went to their brick n mortar store because of the same sizing issue… so it's better if u try it at their offline store and then proceed to purchase” [[rec|dff1e8c42ec7425a8260683d42a33b842ef9265c]]

Variation
- By source:
  - Price (C6) is raised most often on the Play Store relative to its denominator, and also shows up on Reddit and YouTube; App Store mentions are present but fewer. [[analysis_source_code|play|C6]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C6]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C6]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C6]]
  - Fit & size uncertainty (C1) is discussed most on YouTube relative to its denominator, and is lower on Reddit, App Store, and especially low on the Play Store. [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C1]]
- Co-occurrence patterns:
  - C1 clusters with external validation & social proof (C10) and styling & self-image (C3). [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C10]] [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C3]]
  - C6 clusters with action trigger (C13) and external validation & social proof (C11). [[analysis_cooccurrence|C13|C6]] [[analysis_cooccurrence|C11|C6]]
- Interpretation: For C4, C5, C7, and D1 the corpus is too thin to rank or to assess cross-source consistency; we mention their co-occurrence when relevant but do not compare prevalence. [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]]

- Material & digital-physical gap (C2) is discussed more often than either C6 or C1, at 241 of 1018 records. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]]
- Styling & self-image (C3) is also common at 154 of 1018, and appears with C1 in 40 joint records and with C6 in 23, indicating overlapping reasons rather than single-cause explanations. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]] [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C3]] [[analysis_cooccurrence|C3|C6]]

Confidence
Medium. Both C1 and C6 have reliable agreement with a human coder (kappa 0.657 for C1; 0.645 for C6). [[analysis_gold_agreement|C1]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C6]] However, two validation thresholds fail at the metric level and estimated relevance recall is below the target, which tempers confidence. [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]]

Limitations
- This is discussion share, not a funnel metric: counts reflect how often people who chose to post raised a barrier, not how many shoppers did or did not convert. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]]
- The relevance rubric is narrow and may under-represent price/value and delivery/trust topics; rankings are conditional on that filter. [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]]
- Only about 36% of records are Myntra-specific; most discussion is about Indian online fashion generally, so Myntra-targeted claims rest on a smaller base. [[analysis_method_flags|myntra_specific_share]]
- App-store sources are not independent from each other and carry review-skew; the corpus reflects roughly three independent source types. [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]]
- Segments are derived from codes, so any lift of confidence-phase barriers into undecided segments is partly circular. [[analysis_method_flags|segments_derived_not_observed]]
- Price (C6) is constrained: project rules disallow solving via discounts; interpret prevalence as a need for transparency, anchoring, or timing rather than price cuts. [[analysis_method_flags|no_monetary_incentive]]
- Small-n topics cannot be ranked; co-occurrences are reported but thin areas like C4, C5, C7, D1 should not be over-interpreted. [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]]

results.question: Are people who wishlist actually intending to buy, or just bookmarking?
results.restated: Do people who add items to wishlists actually intend to buy those items, or are they primarily using wishlists as bookmarks/reference shelves?
results.answer:
Answer
Many wishlisters appear to have purchase intent: only a small share explicitly say intent never existed, while larger shares talk about price, fit/size, validation, and post-save second thoughts as the reasons they don’t buy, often alongside workarounds that indicate ongoing intent [[analysis_code_prevalence|C9]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]] [[analysis_workaround|C6]] [[analysis_workaround|C1]] [[analysis_workaround|C4]] [[analysis_workaround|C13]]. At the same time, there is a real “bookmarking” cohort saving for reference, not purchase [[analysis_addressable|collectors]].

Evidence
- Intent never existed: C9 appears in 21 of 1,018 relevant records (share 0.021) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C9]].
- Intent extinguished after saving: C12 appears in 54 of 1,018 (share 0.053) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]].
- Bookmarking/taste-archive behaviour: Collectors segment is 126 of 1,018 (share 0.124) — sized to show how much wishlisting is not intent [[analysis_addressable|collectors]].
- Barriers discussed alongside wishlists:
  - Price (timing/value): C6 appears in 207 of 1,018 (share 0.203) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]].
  - Fit & size uncertainty: C1 appears in 189 of 1,018 (share 0.186) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]].
  - External validation via reviews: C4 appears in 82 of 1,018 (share 0.081) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]].
  - Action trigger/timing: C13 appears in 51 of 1,018 (share 0.05) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C13]].
- Workarounds/follow-ups (evidence of continued intent):
  - Action trigger: 11 of 49 C13 records with a workaround (share 0.224) [[analysis_workaround|C13]].
  - Reviews/social proof: 17 of 77 C4 records with a workaround (share 0.221) [[analysis_workaround|C4]].
  - Price timing/value checks: 30 of 201 C6 records with a workaround (share 0.149) [[analysis_workaround|C6]].
  - Fit checks: 17 of 177 C1 records with a workaround (share 0.096) [[analysis_workaround|C1]].
- Counterfactual purchase statements:
  - Action trigger: 12 of 49 C13 records include explicit counterfactuals (share 0.245) [[analysis_counterfactuals|C13]].
  - Intent extinguished: 8 of 52 C12 records include counterfactuals (share 0.154) [[analysis_counterfactuals|C12]].
  - Never intended: 0 of 20 C9 records include counterfactuals (share 0) [[analysis_counterfactuals|C9]].

In users' words
- “I was cleaning my wishlist yesterday and realised half the clothes I save are not for anything I actually have planned” [[rec|6102d72a4134c75fd1e23e0da192954f39145fbd]].
- “I can’t go into Marks and Spencer’s pick up my size and walk out without even trying it on because i know it will fit.” [[rec|8dc9f620df57ba31889994d52e9f60eddacf3fd3]].

- “first see how many posts, comments and reviews did it get and then go ahead” [[rec|0afe1663f365d89029adf08a61c57bd3b6f623c7]].

Variation
- By source platform:

- By segment:
  - Lapsed Intenders: C12 appears in 54 of 78 (share 0.692) [[analysis_segment_recommendation|2]].
  - Hesitant Waiters: C6 in 77 of 108 (share 0.712) and C13 in 27 of 108 (share 0.25) [[analysis_segment_recommendation|6]].
  - Stuck Deciders: Fit/size (C1) in 159 of 392 (share 0.405) [[analysis_segment_recommendation|4]].

- Other confidence-phase doubts are raised more often than never-intended and can stall purchase: the gap between how an item looks online and in person (C2) appears in 241 of 1,018 (share 0.237) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]]; styling & self-image (C3) in 154 of 1,018 (share 0.151) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]]; fulfilment/returns pain (C7) in 140 of 1,018 (share 0.138) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]]; and external validation & social proof (C10) in 68 of 1,018 (share 0.067) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C10]]. Medium. Two high-prevalence drivers (price C6 and fit C1) have reliable coder agreement (kappa 0.64–0.66) [[analysis_gold_agreement|C6]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C1]]. However, several key indicators (C4, C13) have unmeasured reliability, and two validation thresholds fail at the corpus level (recall estimate and per-code kappa coverage) [[analysis_gold_agreement|C4]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C13]] [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]].

- The corpus measures discussion, not behavior: shares are how often people raise a point, not conversion or abandonment rates [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]].
- Coverage is narrow relative to the full “save-to-purchase” journey; relevance recall is estimated below target and likely under-represents price/value and delivery/trust topics [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]].

results.question: What needs keep coming up that nothing currently meets?
results.restated: Which shopper needs are repeatedly raised in the corpus as unmet by current wishlist/checkout experiences on Indian online fashion platforms?
results.answer:
Answer
Across saved-to-buy discussions, the biggest unmet needs people raise are: the gap between how an item looks online and in person (C2), price (C6), fit & size uncertainty (C1), styling & self-image (C3), fulfilment (returns/friction) (C7), and external validation via reviews (C4) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]]. These often combine rather than appearing alone, especially product-clarity with reviews and returns, and fit with needing a second opinion [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C4]][[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C7]][[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C10]].

Evidence
- The gap between how an item looks online and in person (C2): 241 of 1,018 records; 226 distinct authors; spread across 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]].
- Price (C6): 207 of 1,018; 189 distinct authors; 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]].
- Fit & size uncertainty (C1): 189 of 1,018; 185 distinct authors; 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]].
- Styling & self-image (C3): 154 of 1,018; 142 distinct authors; 3 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]].
- Fulfilment (C7): 140 of 1,018; 137 distinct authors; 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]].
- External validation via reviews (C4): 82 of 1,018; 80 distinct authors; 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]].

Source spread highlights
- C2 appears on YouTube 116/573 (share 0.202), Reddit 104/309 (share 0.337), Play 18/114 (share 0.158), App Store 3/22 (share 0.136) [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C2]][[analysis_source_code|reddit|C2]][[analysis_source_code|play|C2]][[analysis_source_code|appstore|C2]].
- C6 appears on Reddit 74/309 (share 0.239), YouTube 70/573 (share 0.122), Play 60/114 (share 0.526), App Store 3/22 (share 0.136) [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C6]][[analysis_source_code|youtube|C6]][[analysis_source_code|play|C6]][[analysis_source_code|appstore|C6]].
- C1 appears on YouTube 144/573 (share 0.251), Reddit 40/309 (share 0.129), Play 3/114 (share 0.026), App Store 2/22 (share 0.091) [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C1]][[analysis_source_code|reddit|C1]][[analysis_source_code|play|C1]][[analysis_source_code|appstore|C1]].
- C3 appears on Reddit 99/309 (share 0.32), YouTube 53/573 (share 0.092), Play 2/114 (share 0.018) [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C3]][[analysis_source_code|youtube|C3]][[analysis_source_code|play|C3]].
- C4 appears on YouTube 43/573 (share 0.075), Reddit 33/309 (share 0.107), App Store 3/22 (share 0.136), Play 3/114 (share 0.026) [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C4]][[analysis_source_code|reddit|C4]][[analysis_source_code|appstore|C4]][[analysis_source_code|play|C4]].

In users' words
- Fit & size uncertainty (C1) and fulfilment (C7) workaround: “it’s better if u try it at their offline store and then proceed to purchase” [[rec|dff1e8c42ec7425a8260683d42a33b842ef9265c]].
- Price timing (C6) and decision deferral: “Omggg I was just now adding things to my cart for the B1G1 sale 😭😭 Thank goddddd I check Reddit before ordering from these new stores.” [[rec|b515b6c496b3bf94f2fba6fd110447c1537ac47c]].
- Product clarity (C2) and returns trust (C7): “I’ve bought clothes online from e-commerce stores like Ajio, myntra and it’s been good experience since they’ve return policy....” [[rec|8c0d0711c1c6335c7098f3425e1764d818b4ca46]].
- Styling & self-image rule (C3): “If I cannot make 4 outfits using the top/bottom I want with what I already have, it needs to go.” [[rec|7eba34c5ff8513db5733b5a039db458d44021226]].

Variation
- By source, styling & self-image (C3) is raised more on Reddit 99/309 (share 0.32) than on YouTube 53/573 (share 0.092) or Play 2/114 (share 0.018) [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C3]][[analysis_source_code|youtube|C3]][[analysis_source_code|play|C3]].
- Price (C6) shows a strong presence in Play Store reviews 60/114 (share 0.526) compared with YouTube 70/573 (share 0.122) and Reddit 74/309 (share 0.239) [[analysis_source_code|play|C6]][[analysis_source_code|youtube|C6]][[analysis_source_code|reddit|C6]].
- Fit & size uncertainty (C1) is more often raised on YouTube 144/573 (share 0.251) than on Reddit 40/309 (share 0.129) or Play 3/114 (share 0.026) [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C1]][[analysis_source_code|reddit|C1]][[analysis_source_code|play|C1]].

Counter-evidence
- Other, smaller but present rivals at the same stage: external validation & social proof (need to check with others) (C10) 68/1,018; intent extinguished after saving (C12) 54/1,018; action trigger/timing (C13) 51/1,018; external validation elsewhere (go check properly somewhere else) (C14) 38/1,018; availability at decision time (C8) 35/1,018 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C10]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C13]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C14]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C8]].
- These needs frequently co-occur rather than stand alone: the product look/feel gap (C2) with reviews (C4) appears together in 53 records; C2 with fulfilment (C7) in 65; fit & size (C1) with checking with others (C10) in 37; intent extinguished (C12) with styling (C3) in 22; action trigger (C13) with styling (C3) in 22 [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C4]][[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C7]][[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C10]][[analysis_cooccurrence|C12|C3]][[analysis_cooccurrence|C13|C3]].

Confidence
- Agreement with the human coder is strong for fit & size uncertainty (C1) and price (C6), with kappa 0.66 and 0.64 respectively (verdict: reliable) [[analysis_gold_agreement|C1]][[analysis_gold_agreement|C6]].
- Product look/feel gap (C2) and styling & self-image (C3) have weaker agreement (kappa 0.43 and 0.52; verdict: weak), so their exact ordering should be treated as provisional [[analysis_gold_agreement|C2]][[analysis_gold_agreement|C3]].
- Reviews (C4) and fulfilment (C7) are not measurable on gold (too few gold labels), so reliability is unknown [[analysis_gold_agreement|C4]][[analysis_gold_agreement|C7]].
- Method-level caveats apply: two validation thresholds fail; every share is a share of discussion, not a conversion rate; app-store sources are not independent types [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]][[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]][[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]].
Overall confidence: Medium — strong counts across multiple sources, but with mixed reliability across codes and known method flags [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]][[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]][[analysis_gold_agreement|C1]][[analysis_gold_agreement|C2]][[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]].

Limitations
- The corpus measures what people say, not what they do; no funnel or conversion data exists here [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]].
- The relevance rubric is narrow; a hand-read sample suggested lower recall for price/trust/fulfilment content, so rankings reflect stated barriers under this rubric rather than all decision-relevant talk [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]].
- Only about 36% of relevant discussion is Myntra-specific; many findings generalize to Indian fashion e-commerce rather than to Myntra alone [[analysis_method_flags|myntra_specific_share]].
- Some codes have weak or unknown reliability on gold (C2, C3 weak; C4, C7 not measurable), so their precise positions should be read cautiously [[analysis_gold_agreement|C2]][[analysis_gold_agreement|C3]][[analysis_gold_agreement|C4]][[analysis_gold_agreement|C7]].
- App-store reviews share a source-type bias, so “triangulation across four sources” overstates independence; effectively three independent source types [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]].
- Price (C6) cannot be directly solved with monetary incentives under project constraints; interpret it as a need for transparency/anchoring/timing, not an argument for price cuts [[analysis_method_flags|no_monetary_incentive]].
- Segments (e.g., “undecided”) are derived from classification rules, not observed behavior; any lift into such segments is partly circular [[analysis_method_flags|segments_derived_not_observed]].
- Counts below typical floors are reportable but not rankable; read smaller codes like C8 with that context [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]].

results.question: What is the return policy on Myntra right now?
results.restated: What is Myntra's current return policy?
results.answer:
Answer
Correction: This corpus contains user discussion about wishlist barriers and does not contain up-to-date corporate policy documents; it cannot reliably state Myntra's current return policy. For the current policy, consult Myntra's official website, app help/returns section, or customer support. Interpretation: What we can report is that users frequently frame returns/exchanges as part of Fulfilment (C7) and sometimes complain about Late-revealed terms (D3), but this is discussion, not official policy.

Evidence
- Fulfilment (returns/exchanges logistics and pain) appears in discussion across sources: 67 of 573 YouTube records, 46 of 309 Reddit records, 22 of 114 Google Play records, and 5 of 22 App Store records discuss C7 [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C7]], [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C7]], [[analysis_source_code|play|C7]], [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C7]].
- Late-revealed terms (unexpected after-purchase constraints like no returns or account blocks) are present but thinner: 13 of 114 Google Play records, 6 of 573 YouTube records, 6 of 309 Reddit records, and 1 of 22 App Store records discuss D3 [[analysis_source_code|play|D3]], [[analysis_source_code|youtube|D3]], [[analysis_source_code|reddit|D3]], [[analysis_source_code|appstore|D3]].
- Required gap to name: D3 is under the 15-record floor for rankable, cross-source claims; a count below 15 is “not shown as a finding at all” [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]].

In users' words
- “exchange and return policy is far better than myntra” [[rec|84644fbcb42a7cef2df5f6eaec320b472a23d89c]]
- “they didn't even replace shoes which was not fitting well, saying I have used it. The policies need improvement.” [[rec|48ca0d850554f6bef58eb9d929de13797b53a9f0]]
- “there is no return or exchange option available for this product.” [[rec|893ede648353cc8d160309de57577ec7530ce63a]]
- “they block your account because of maximum return or refund” [[rec|8fd21b8675408547e3337ba6c3783cfea03e86ef]]

Variation
- By source, Fulfilment (C7) is discussed across all four sources with per-source counts and denominators: YouTube 67/573, Reddit 46/309, Google Play 22/114, App Store 5/22 [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C7]], [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C7]], [[analysis_source_code|play|C7]], [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C7]].
- By source, Late-revealed terms (D3) are present but thinner everywhere: Google Play 13/114, YouTube 6/573, Reddit 6/309, App Store 1/22 [[analysis_source_code|play|D3]], [[analysis_source_code|youtube|D3]], [[analysis_source_code|reddit|D3]], [[analysis_source_code|appstore|D3]].
- Interpretation: Because every per-source D3 count is below the 15-record floor, we cannot make a robust across-source claim for D3; it remains directional only [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]].

Counter-evidence
- Other rival barriers are also prominent in discussion: the gap between how an item looks online and in person (C2) appears in 241 of 1018 records; Price (C6) in 207 of 1018; Fit & size uncertainty (C1) in 189 of 1018; Styling & self-image (C3) in 154 of 1018; External validation & social proof (C4) in 82 of 1018 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]], [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]], [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]], [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]], [[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]].
- C7 often co-occurs with C2, suggesting returns/exchanges concerns are frequently raised alongside product-looks-vs-photos doubts, not as a sole cause (65 joint mentions; relationship measure provided in the row) [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C7]].

Confidence
- Low. Reliability for C7 and D3 is “not measurable” due to too few gold labels; their agreement statistics are reported as unknown rather than strong or poor [[analysis_gold_agreement|C7]], [[analysis_gold_agreement|D3]]. Two validation thresholds fail overall, so metrics should be read with caution [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]]. Only about 36% of relevant discussion is Myntra-specific, which narrows the directly-applicable base [[analysis_method_flags|myntra_specific_share]]. App-store sources are not independent of each other, reducing triangulation strength [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]].

Limitations
- This is discussion, not behavior: every share here is how often people chose to raise an issue, not a conversion or return rate [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]].
- The relevance rubric is narrow; excluded material skews toward price/value and delivery-and-trust, so rankings reflect a constrained lens on decision barriers [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]].
- Two validation thresholds fail; per-code agreement is strong for only a subset of codes, reducing certainty [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]].
- Only about 36% of relevant records are Myntra-specific; platform-mechanical readings rest on a smaller Myntra pool [[analysis_method_flags|myntra_specific_share]].
- App-store reviews share source-type biases and are not independent of each other [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]].
- Counts below 15 are not claimable as findings; D3 per-source counts are below this floor, so cross-source robustness for late-revealed terms cannot be established here [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]], [[analysis_source_code|play|D3]], [[analysis_source_code|youtube|D3]], [[analysis_source_code|reddit|D3]], [[analysis_source_code|appstore|D3]].

Interpretation: To proceed, please clarify whether you want the general returns policy or rules for a specific category; whether you need the latest version or a policy as of a specific date; whether you want granular rules (time windows, refund vs. replacement, exceptions) or a high-level summary; and whether only official text will do or a user-reported summary is acceptable.

In users' words
- "there is no return or exchange option available for this product." [[rec|893ede648353cc8d160309de57577ec7530ce63a]]
- "easy returns" [[rec|a5d9980f7efb299432d0c13cac8c38e1603912cc]]

- Two validation thresholds failed at the corpus level, including relevance recall below target, which reduces confidence in precise prevalence comparisons [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]].

results.question: Do users trust influencer reviews?
results.restated: Do people in the corpus express trust or distrust in influencer reviews when deciding whether to buy wishlist items on Indian online fashion platforms?
results.answer:
Answer
Interpretation: The corpus does not separate influencer content from ordinary buyer reviews, so it cannot directly answer whether people trust influencer reviews; it only shows that people discuss external validation (reviews/testimonials and off‑platform checks) as part of their decision-making. Within that, users do talk about needing reviews and sometimes preferring offline checks before buying wishlist items.

Evidence
- External validation & social proof — What did people who actually received it say? (C4): 82 of 1018 posts [[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]]; by source: 43 of 573 on YouTube, 33 of 309 on Reddit, 3 of 22 on the App Store, and 3 of 114 on Google Play [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C4]], [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C4]], [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C4]], [[analysis_source_code|play|C4]].
- External validation & social proof — Let me go check this properly somewhere else (C14): 38 of 1018 posts [[analysis_code_prevalence|C14]]; by source: 19 of 309 on Reddit, 17 of 573 on YouTube, 1 of 22 on the App Store, and 1 of 114 on Google Play [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C14]], [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C14]], [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C14]], [[analysis_source_code|play|C14]].
- Co-occurrence with the gap between how an item looks online and in person (C2): C2 co-occurs with C4 in 53 posts (lift 2.73) and with fulfilment (C7) in 65 posts (lift 1.961) [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C4]], [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C7]].
- Comparison & decision load (C5) is sparse at 22 of 1018, so any cross-source breakouts for this topic are too thin to rely on [[analysis_code_prevalence|C5]].

In users' words
- “Bro in Ajio app there is no customer rating & reviews option?then how can we know that products are quality or not? without reviews?” [[rec|aea48d3f4b52061090c5e983ad2790dd364cab14]]
- “solution read product reviews then buy.” [[rec|45a8341fa1843b03574e839eed8ea6a7c902f9b8]]
- “Would definitely help a lot. But I would prefer local shops and street shopping, so so much better” [[rec|0afe1663f365d89029adf08a61c57bd3b6f623c7]]
- “The product descriptions and reviews are helpful when deciding what to buy” [[rec|f6ae686daf77f145709f48d4315dc6c4b9773a74]]

Variation
- By source, discussions of “what people who actually received it say” (C4) appear on YouTube (43 of 573), Reddit (33 of 309), the App Store (3 of 22), and Google Play (3 of 114) [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C4]], [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C4]], [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C4]], [[analysis_source_code|play|C4]].
- Off‑platform verification (C14) shows Reddit (19 of 309) and YouTube (17 of 573), with single-digit counts on the app stores [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C14]], [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C14]], [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C14]], [[analysis_source_code|play|C14]].
- Interpretation: Because influencer content is not separated from buyer reviews, the corpus cannot tell whether influencer‑trust comments are concentrated on particular platforms.

Counter-evidence
- Rival barriers are discussed more often than C4/C14: the gap between how an item looks online and in person (C2) appears in 241 of 1018 posts [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]], price (C6) in 207 of 1018 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]], styling & self-image (C3) in 154 of 1018 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]], and fulfilment (C7) in 140 of 1018 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]]. This shows many conversations focus on factors other than reviews.

Confidence
Medium-Low. C4 and C14 are the closest available proxies to “influencer trust,” but both have limited reliability statistics (C4 and C14 are “not measurable” for agreement), and C2 — which co-occurs with C4 — has weak agreement (kappa 0.427) [[analysis_gold_agreement|C4]], [[analysis_gold_agreement|C14]], [[analysis_gold_agreement|C2]]. Overall method thresholds also failed on two metrics [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]]. Still, counts draw on multiple source types [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C4]], [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C4]], [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C4]], [[analysis_source_code|play|C4]], which supports basic directional reading.

Limitations
- Interpretation: The corpus does not separate influencer content from ordinary buyer reviews, so any statement about “influencer trust” is inferred from broader external‑validation talk (C4, C14), not measured directly.
- Shares are of discussion, not shopper behavior; no funnel data exists [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]].
- Validation thresholds failed and per‑code agreement is limited for several relevant codes [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]].
- The relevance rubric is narrow; price/value and delivery‑and‑trust topics may be underrepresented, so rankings are conditional on what was included [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]].
- Only about 36% of the corpus is Myntra‑specific; much discussion is about Indian online fashion generally [[analysis_method_flags|myntra_specific_share]].
- Segments are derived from codes and are not independent behavioral groups [[analysis_method_flags|segments_derived_not_observed]].
- Source independence is limited to roughly three types (YouTube, Reddit, app stores), and app‑store reviews have known skews [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]].
- Some breakouts are below the minimum n to rank confidently (e.g., C5 at 22 of 1018) [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]], [[analysis_code_prevalence|C5]].

Sub-questions addressed
- How often do posts explicitly mention influencer reviews as trustworthy or untrustworthy? Interpretation: No explicit influencer‑specific mentions were retrieved; users speak about “reviews,” “customer testimonials,” and off‑platform checks in general, not influencers per se [[rec|aea48d3f4b52061090c5e983ad2790dd364cab14]], [[rec|0afe1663f365d89029adf08a61c57bd3b6f623c7]], [[rec|f6ae686daf77f145709f48d4315dc6c4b9773a74]], [[rec|45a8341fa1843b03574e839eed8ea6a7c902f9b8]].
- Are influencer-trust comments concentrated on particular platforms? Interpretation: Not answerable — influencer content is not separated; available platform splits cover general review‑seeking (C4, C14) [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C4]], [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C4]], [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C14]], [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C14]].
- When influencer reviews are distrusted, what alternative evidence do people seek? Users ask for customer ratings/reviews, product descriptions, and off‑platform or in‑person checks: “no customer rating & reviews option?” [[rec|aea48d3f4b52061090c5e983ad2790dd364cab14]], “The product descriptions and reviews are helpful” [[rec|f6ae686daf77f145709f48d4315dc6c4b9773a74]], “I would prefer local shops and street shopping” [[rec|0afe1663f365d89029adf08a61c57bd3b6f623c7]].
- Do influencer-review doubts co-occur with other barriers? Interpretation: Using external validation (C4) as the nearest proxy, discussions co‑occur with the gap between how an item looks online and in person (C2) in 53 posts and with fulfilment (C7) in 65 posts [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C4]], [[analysis_cooccurrence|C2|C7]].
- How many posts state they would have bought if a trusted influencer had endorsed the item? Interpretation: Not observed in the retrieved records; no explicit counterfactual about influencer endorsement appears in the quotes or counts above.
gate_reasons: the corpus does not separate influencer content from ordinary buyer reviews
gate_caveats: whether this holds up across sources: too thin to report for C5

results.question: What do shoppers in Bangalore think about wishlist pricing?
results.restated: What do shoppers in Bangalore think about wishlist pricing?
results.answer:
Answer
Interpretation: The corpus cannot report what “Bangalore shoppers” think — it has no location fields — so we can only summarise how wishlist pricing shows up in the overall discussion and whether any records happen to mention Bangalore would need a manual check. Price (C6) is a common discussion barrier in the corpus, while cost surprise (D1) and other adjacent themes appear less often and/or are too thin to generalise across sources.

Evidence
- Price (C6): 207 of 1018 records, from 189 distinct authors, across 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]].
- Social proof (C4): 82 of 1018, 80 distinct authors, 4 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]].
- Intent extinguished after saving (C12): 54 of 1018, 49 distinct authors, 3 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]].
- Action trigger (C13): 51 of 1018, 50 distinct authors, 3 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|C13]].
- Cost surprise (D1): 14 of 1018, 14 distinct authors, 3 sources [[analysis_code_prevalence|D1]].
- Source mix for price (C6): Reddit 74/309; YouTube 70/573; Play 60/114; App Store 3/22 [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C6]], [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C6]], [[analysis_source_code|play|C6]], [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C6]].
- Counterfactual mentions tied to price (C6): 31 counterfactuals out of 201 C6-coded records [[analysis_counterfactuals|C6]].
- Rival barriers in the same stage: Material & digital-physical gap (C2) 241/1018; Fit & size uncertainty (C1) 189/1018; Styling & self-image (C3) 154/1018; Fulfilment (C7) 140/1018; External validation (C10) 68/1018 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]], [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]], [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]], [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]], [[analysis_code_prevalence|C10]].
- Reliability: C6 clears agreement threshold (kappa 0.645) [[analysis_gold_agreement|C6]].

In users' words
- “many products on Myntra has higher pricing for M too” [[rec|276f3f42326dc46e1fb820fce423992f9d19c3b8]].
- “not regret paying the price you paid. Sometimes pricing is different for a reason.” [[rec|65eda089bf4a51cec257c0804e9741d27e6c46b4]].
- “If you’re confused, don’t buy anything right now.” [[rec|68a019b5c3cfee99b74063996b32854283136a57]].
- “first see how many posts, comments and reviews did it get” [[rec|0afe1663f365d89029adf08a61c57bd3b6f623c7]].

Variation
- Interpretation: No geographic data was collected, so there is no Bangalore-specific breakdown.
- By source for price (C6): Reddit 74/309; YouTube 70/573; Play 60/114; App Store 3/22 — discussion of price appears across all four sources, with notably high share on Google Play among its smaller denominator [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C6]], [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C6]], [[analysis_source_code|play|C6]], [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C6]]. Interpretation: Because Google Play and the App Store share app‑review skews, “four sources” reduce to roughly three independent source types [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]], and store scraping contributes volume disproportionate to signal [[analysis_method_flags|store_scrape_low_yield]].
- Interpretation: Whether patterns hold across sources is too thin to report for D1, C5, C12, C13 as flagged.

Counter-evidence
- Other barriers are discussed at least as often or more than price: Material & digital-physical gap (C2) 241/1018 and Fit & size uncertainty (C1) 189/1018, among others [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]], [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]], [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]], [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]].
- Price (C6) commonly co-occurs with other needs, suggesting it is not a single-cause explanation: it appears with action trigger (C13) in 20 joint records and with another code in notable pairs [[analysis_cooccurrence|C13|C6]].
- Counterfactuals tied to price (31 out of 201 C6-coded) indicate mixed sentiments and that some users frame price conditions under which they would act, which contradicts a blanket “wishlist pricing is the sole blocker” reading [[analysis_counterfactuals|C6]].

Confidence
- Medium. Price (C6) coding is reliable (kappa 0.645) [[analysis_gold_agreement|C6]], but overall validation thresholds fail on other metrics [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]]. Source independence is limited to roughly three types [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]].

Limitations
- Interpretation: No geography or location fields exist in the corpus, so we cannot isolate Bangalore or count Bangalore-specific authors; any claim about “Bangalore shoppers” is unverifiable here.
- All numbers are shares of discussion, not behaviour or conversion metrics [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]].
- The relevance rubric is narrow and may under-represent price/value and delivery‑trust topics, so barrier ranking is conditional [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]].
- Only about 36% of the relevant corpus is Myntra-specific; much of the discussion is about Indian online fashion generally [[analysis_method_flags|myntra_specific_share]].
- Some codes (e.g., D1, C5, C12, C13) are thin and/or not measurably reliable, so cross-source generalisation is limited [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]].
- The project constraint means price (C6) cannot be addressed by discounts; interpret C6 through transparency, anchoring and timing rather than monetary incentives [[analysis_method_flags|no_monetary_incentive]].

premise.correction: The corpus contains no geography or location fields, so it cannot reliably report opinions specific to Bangalore; we can only report what the corpus as a whole says about wishlist pricing and whether any records happen to mention Bangalore (which would need to be checked).

results.question: Has fit uncertainty got worse over the last two years?
results.restated: Has fit uncertainty (code C1) become more common in discussion over the last two years?
results.answer:
Answer
Correction: The corpus contains no usable time-series population-level measures; it cannot determine whether Fit & size uncertainty (C1) became more or less common over time. Interpretation: What we can report is its current share of discussion and how that varies by source, not a trend over the last two years.

Evidence
- Current prevalence: Fit & size uncertainty (C1) appears in 189 of 1018 records, from 185 distinct authors, across 4 sources; mean classifier confidence 0.816 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]].
- By source (shares are of each source’s relevant records):
  - YouTube: 144 of 573 (n_distinct_authors=143) [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C1]].
  - Reddit: 40 of 309 (n_distinct_authors=37) [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C1]].
  - Google Play: 3 of 114 (n_distinct_authors=3) [[analysis_source_code|play|C1]].
  - App Store: 2 of 22 (n_distinct_authors=2) [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C1]].
- Rival barriers (same stage) for context:
  - Material & digital-physical gap (C2): 241 of 1018 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]].
  - Price (C6): 207 of 1018 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]].
  - Styling & self-image (C3): 154 of 1018 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]].
  - Fulfilment (C7): 140 of 1018 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]].
  - External validation & social proof (C4): 82 of 1018 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]].

Interpretation: The corpus was collected in a single window; it does not report dates or counts by month/quarter, and it cannot show a before/after pattern. Therefore, none of the sub-questions that require time-slicing (time coverage, distinct authors per period, robustness of any change over time, or whether changes could be sampling artefacts) can be answered from this data.

In users' words
- “I already know my fit, size & what I’m getting” [[rec|55600249871014f148b2ab06d18f96f3fe93c191]].
- “First and last time ordered” [[rec|ac309714d865aa6bef9d4eae722713ba917a9f7e]].

Variation
- By source, Fit & size uncertainty (C1) is discussed at different levels: 144/573 on YouTube, 40/309 on Reddit, 3/114 on Google Play, and 2/22 on the App Store [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C1]].
- Interpretation: Whether any time trend would be robust to source composition cannot be assessed; the dataset lacks time coverage and period-by-source breakdowns needed to separate content mix shifts from real change over time.
- Interpretation: Whether this holds up across sources is too thin to report for C2, C4, C5, C6, C7 (the brief flags this gap explicitly).

Counter-evidence
- Other confidence-phase barriers also account for substantial discussion, including Material & digital-physical gap (241/1018) and Styling & self-image (154/1018), indicating that Fit & size uncertainty is one of several prominent topics rather than a solitary driver [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]].
- Co-occurrence shows Fit & size uncertainty (C1) often appears alongside External validation & social proof (C10), with 37 joint records; this suggests fit concerns are sometimes entangled with social approval needs, not standalone causes [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C10]].

Confidence
- Medium. C1’s classifier agreement with a human coder clears the 0.60 kappa threshold (kappa 0.657; verdict “reliable”) [[analysis_gold_agreement|C1]]. However, two validation thresholds fail at the corpus level, and relevance recall is estimated at about 79% vs an 85% threshold, which lowers overall confidence in fine-grained comparisons [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]]. Source diversity is present but reflects roughly three independent source types, not four [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]].

Limitations
- Interpretation: No trend inference — the corpus was collected in a single window and provides no time-series counts; it cannot answer “has C1 increased over two years?” (the central gap the brief requires naming).
- Every share reported is a share of discussion, not a behavioral rate; no funnel or user-level data exists here [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]].
- Relevance rubric is narrow; on a hand-read sample, implied recall was near 45%, with exclusions skewing toward price/value and delivery/trust, so barrier rankings reflect a constrained slice of discussion [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]].
- Validation thresholds: only 2 of 5 measurable codes clear kappa 0.60; relevance recall below target further constrains certainty [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]].
- App-store sources have low signal yield and shared biases; treat per-source contrasts with caution [[analysis_method_flags|store_scrape_low_yield]] [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]].
- Only about 36% of relevant records are Myntra-specific; most evidence concerns Indian online fashion generally, limiting Myntra-specific conclusions [[analysis_method_flags|myntra_specific_share]].
- Some low-n cells (e.g., C1 on App Store and Play) are below the floor for ranking; they are reportable but not robust for ordering [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]].
- Segments are derived from codes, not observed behavior, so any segment-level lift for confidence-phase barriers is partly circular [[analysis_method_flags|segments_derived_not_observed]].
