results.question: Which specific brands do people say run small?
results.restated: Which specific brands do people say run small on Indian online fashion platforms?
results.answer:
Answer
Interpretation: Correction — the corpus has no structured brand fields or reliable brand-level metadata, so it cannot tell us which specific brands “run small.” It can only speak to fit & size uncertainty in aggregate and how often it is raised across sources.

Evidence
- Fit & size uncertainty (C1) appears in 189 of 1018 records (n=189/1018) across 4 sources, with mean coder confidence 0.816 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]].
- By source for C1:
  - YouTube: 144 of 573 (n=144/573) [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C1]]
  - Reddit: 40 of 309 (n=40/309) [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C1]]
  - Google Play: 3 of 114 (n=3/114) [[analysis_source_code|play|C1]]
  - App Store: 2 of 22 (n=2/22) [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C1]]
- Co-occurrence around C1:
  - With External validation & social proof (C10): 37 joint mentions (n_joint=37) [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C10]]
  - With Styling & self-image (C3): 40 joint mentions (n_joint=40) [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C3]]
  - With Material & digital-physical gap (C2): 25 joint mentions (n_joint=25) [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C2]]
  - With Fulfilment (C7): 16 joint mentions (n_joint=16) [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C7]]

In users' words
- “brand size small 36,medium=38,large=40” [[rec|b951e8a49b705356628dd51c12fa274f58375393]]
- “I had to replace the product due to it being small in size” [[rec|4ffd2cedd58c1994e04a39df72f3e0bc874874c1]]
- “Levi’s jeans is constant.” [[rec|c5206d8f73af2e9a7d2d0a89dd3237df7576b712]]
- “Pagla ajio ma armani hugo Boss            Jimmy choo bara bara brand ha” [[rec|fbcf7a08191364e0a6a958e65cd039904a909502]]

Variation
- By source, fit & size uncertainty (C1) is raised most on YouTube (n=144/573) and also appears on Reddit (n=40/309), with smaller counts on Google Play (n=3/114) and the App Store (n=2/22) [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C1]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C1]].
- Interpretation: Whether brand-size complaints vary similarly for review-driven sources or for fulfilment/returns topics is too thin to report for C4, D3, and C7 as a source-level pattern per the brief.

Counter-evidence
- Other barriers are raised as often or more than fit & size uncertainty:
  - The gap between how an item looks online and in person (C2): 241 of 1018 (n=241/1018) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]]
  - Price (C6): 207 of 1018 (n=207/1018) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]]
  - Styling & self-image (C3): 154 of 1018 (n=154/1018) [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]]
- C1 often appears alongside External validation & social proof (C10) with 37 joint mentions [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C10]], suggesting fit worries are discussed with checking others’ views, rather than only with returns or delivery terms; C1 co-occurs with Fulfilment (C7) 16 times [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C7]].

Confidence
- Medium. Fit & size uncertainty (C1) has strong volume (n=189) and cleared inter-rater reliability (kappa 0.657) [[analysis_gold_agreement|C1]]. However, brand-level conclusions are unsupported by the data structure (Interpretation) and other relevant codes (C4, C7, D3) have unknown reliability [[analysis_gold_agreement|C4]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C7]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|D3]], with method thresholds reported as failing [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]].

Limitations
- Interpretation: No structured brand fields, and the barriers are not classified by brand, so no brand-level comparison exists.
- Shares are of discussion, not shopper behavior; no funnel or conversion data are present [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]].
- The relevance rubric is narrow; recall is estimated below threshold, and exclusions likely skew toward price/value and delivery/trust content [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]].
- Only about 36% of relevant material is Myntra-specific; much of the corpus is about Indian online fashion generally [[analysis_method_flags|myntra_specific_share]].
- Source independence is limited to roughly three source types due to app-store review skew and third-party Reddit access [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]].
- Segment lifts are derived, not observed; associations with “undecided” reflect operationalization choices [[analysis_method_flags|segments_derived_not_observed]].
- For any brand-level claim, we would require verbatim extracts that mention the brand and size concern; counts below 30 are reportable but not rankable, so fewer than 30 brand+size-small records would not support ranking [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]].

Sub-questions
- Does the corpus contain brand names or any structured brand field linked to records?
  - Interpretation: There is no structured brand field; brand mentions appear only ad hoc in text (e.g., “Levi’s,” “ajio … armani hugo Boss … Jimmy choo”) [[rec|c5206d8f73af2e9a7d2d0a89dd3237df7576b712]] [[rec|fbcf7a08191364e0a6a958e65cd039904a909502]].
- If brand mentions exist, how often and in which sources do they appear (per-source counts)?
  - Interpretation: Brand mentions exist sporadically across sources (e.g., YouTube and Reddit, as shown above), but there are no structured per-source brand counts in the corpus to report.
- Are brand-size complaints consistently about fit (C1) rather than returns, availability, or other issues (co-occurrence with other codes)?
  - Interpretation: We cannot isolate brand-size complaints specifically. In aggregate, C1 co-occurs 16 times with Fulfilment (C7) [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C7]] and 25 times with the material/digital-physical gap (C2) [[analysis_cooccurrence|C1|C2]], but this does not separate brand-specific cases.
- Would we require verbatim extracts mentioning brand+size to validate any claim, and what minimum supporting-count would we accept as reliable?
  - Yes: claims would require verbatim brand+size extracts. Counts below 30 are reportable but not rankable; ranking a “runs small” brand would therefore require at least 30 records mentioning that brand-size issue [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]].

results.question: Do people who abandon at checkout come back later?
results.restated: Do people who abandon at checkout (records tagged in the corpus as checkout-stage barriers) later return to complete the purchase or otherwise re-engage with the saved item?
results.answer:
Answer
Partial: We can only speak to what people say about intent around checkout problems, not whether individuals later returned, and the per-source tallies are below the floor to claim consistency. Within that constraint, mentions of checkout-stage abandonment skew toward final exit, with intent sometimes surviving for late reconsideration (D4) and late-revealed terms (D3), evidenced by counterfactuals and some workarounds [[analysis_stage_outcome|D|exit]], [[analysis_counterfactuals|D4]], [[analysis_counterfactuals|D3]], [[analysis_workaround|D3]].

Evidence
- How often checkout-stage outcomes are discussed as exit vs defer:
  - Checkout stage exit: 50 out of 1018 records [[analysis_stage_outcome|D|exit]].
  - Interpretation: No defer row is reported for the checkout stage in the counts provided; the corpus here shows exit mentions but does not report defer mentions at checkout.
- Association between specific checkout barriers and intent surviving (counterfactuals) vs being extinguished:
  - Final reconsideration (D4): 5 counterfactuals out of 9 coded records [[analysis_counterfactuals|D4]].
  - Late-revealed terms (D3): 9 counterfactuals out of 25 coded records [[analysis_counterfactuals|D3]].
  - Mechanical friction (D2): 6 counterfactuals out of 21 coded records [[analysis_counterfactuals|D2]].
  - Cost surprise (D1): 3 counterfactuals out of 14 coded records [[analysis_counterfactuals|D1]].
- Workarounds or alternative behaviors after checkout problems:
  - Late-revealed terms (D3): 7 with workaround out of 25 coded records; mean_effort=1.571 [[analysis_workaround|D3]].
  - Final reconsideration (D4): 2 with workaround out of 9; mean_effort=1 [[analysis_workaround|D4]].
  - Cost surprise (D1): 2 with workaround out of 14; mean_effort=1.5 [[analysis_workaround|D1]].
  - Mechanical friction (D2): 1 with workaround out of 21; mean_effort=2 [[analysis_workaround|D2]].
- Consistency across sources:
  - D3 appears across sources, with counts by source: Play 13 out of 114; YouTube 6 out of 573; Reddit 6 out of 309; App Store 1 out of 22 [[analysis_source_code|play|D3]], [[analysis_source_code|youtube|D3]], [[analysis_source_code|reddit|D3]], [[analysis_source_code|appstore|D3]].
  - D2 appears across sources, with counts by source: YouTube 12 out of 573; Play 8 out of 114; Reddit 1 out of 309; App Store 1 out of 22 [[analysis_source_code|youtube|D2]], [[analysis_source_code|play|D2]], [[analysis_source_code|reddit|D2]], [[analysis_source_code|appstore|D2]].
  - Interpretation: The largest per-source count visible for a checkout barrier is 13, which is below the 15-count floor for claiming stable consistency across sources [[analysis_source_code|play|D3]], [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]].

In users' words
- “it said 15day returns. Now after delivery, I wanted to return some products which didn't fit correctly. So I raised a return request, to which they replied that I need to courier the items to their address and pickup is not available.” [[rec|5938ff20570b551803f9ae3776763181b32e7de1]]
- “pay later option best hai” [[rec|fcaca1d738b9ea244b2a55d43236fef01275e782]]

Variation
- By source, late-revealed terms (D3) show up on Play (13/114), YouTube (6/573), Reddit (6/309), and App Store (1/22), suggesting cross-source presence but at low per-source counts [[analysis_source_code|play|D3]], [[analysis_source_code|youtube|D3]], [[analysis_source_code|reddit|D3]], [[analysis_source_code|appstore|D3]].
- Mechanical friction (D2) is discussed on YouTube (12/573) and Play (8/114), with smaller counts on Reddit (1/309) and App Store (1/22) [[analysis_source_code|youtube|D2]], [[analysis_source_code|play|D2]], [[analysis_source_code|reddit|D2]], [[analysis_source_code|appstore|D2]].
- Interpretation: With the largest per-source count at 13, the corpus is too thin to assert that these patterns are consistent across platforms [[analysis_source_code|play|D3]], [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]].

Counter-evidence
- Much of the discussion is about earlier-stage barriers rather than checkout: price (C6) exit is 207 out of 1018; fulfilment (C7) exit is 140 out of 1018; the gap between how an item looks online and in person (C2) defer is 241 out of 1018; fit & size uncertainty (C1) defer is 189 out of 1018; styling & self-image (C3) defer is 154 out of 1018 [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]], [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]], [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]], [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]], [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]].
- Co-occurrence shows that journey timing (C13) often appears with styling & self-image (C3) and price (C6), indicating overlapping considerations outside checkout: C13 with C3 has n_joint=22; C13 with C6 has n_joint=20 [[analysis_cooccurrence|C13|C3]], [[analysis_cooccurrence|C13|C6]].

Confidence
Low. The checkout codes (D1–D4) have small absolute counts and their reliability against human coding is marked “not measurable,” with too few gold labels per code to interpret agreement statistics [[analysis_gold_agreement|D1]], [[analysis_gold_agreement|D2]], [[analysis_gold_agreement|D3]]. The instrument measures discussion, not behavioral return rates [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]]. Source independence is limited to roughly three source types [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]], and per-source counts fall below the 15-record floor for stable cross-source claims [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]], with the largest per-source checkout barrier count at 13 [[analysis_source_code|play|D3]].

Limitations
- This is discussion, not user- or session-level funnel data; no records are linked to individuals over time, so we cannot observe whether a given person returned later [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]].
- The corpus is not Myntra-specific; about 36% concerns Myntra, so platform-mechanical takeaways rely on a smaller subset [[analysis_method_flags|myntra_specific_share]].
- The relevance rubric is narrow and estimated recall is about 79% against an 85% threshold; excluded material skews toward price/value and delivery/trust, so barrier prominence is conditional on this filter [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]], [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]].
- Per-source counts are below the floor to claim consistency; the top per-source checkout count is 13, under the 15 needed to treat it as stable [[analysis_source_code|play|D3]], [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]].
- App-store sources share similar skews; there are roughly three independent source types, not four [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]].
- Segments are derived from classification rules, not observed behaviors; any lift for “undecided” segments is partly circular [[analysis_method_flags|segments_derived_not_observed]].
- Interpretation: No explicit statements in the retrieved records say that people came back later to complete a purchase after a checkout problem; absence in this sample does not imply impossibility.

[[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]]

There is no code for gift-intent, C10 (the closest adjacent concept) is marked unreliable (kappa 0.10), and overall evaluation thresholds failed on multiple metrics; only 2 of the 5 measurable codes clear kappa 0.60 and estimated relevance recall is about 79%. results.question: Why is price the single biggest barrier to buying wishlisted items?
results.restated: Why is C6 (value & price uncertainty) the single biggest barrier people raise for not buying items they saved to wishlists on Indian online fashion platforms?
results.answer:
Answer
Correction: Price (C6) is not the single biggest barrier in this corpus; Material & digital-physical gap (C2) is raised more often. C6 is, however, a high-prevalence eliminator that appears across sources and includes explicit “would buy if cheaper” counterfactuals. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]]

Evidence
- How often C6 is raised vs. other codes (absolute and share)
  - C2 Material & digital-physical gap: 241 of 1,018 records; share 0.237. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]]
  - C6 Price: 207 of 1,018 records; share 0.203. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]]
  - C1 Fit & size uncertainty: 189 of 1,018 records; share 0.186. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C1]]
  - C3 Styling & self-image: 154 of 1,018 records; share 0.151. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]]
  - C7 Fulfilment: 140 of 1,018 records; share 0.138. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]]
  - C4 External validation & social proof: 82 of 1,018 records; share 0.081. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C4]]
  - C10 External validation & social proof: 68 of 1,018 records; share 0.067. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C10]]
  - C12 Intent extinguished after saving: 54 of 1,018 records; share 0.053. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]]
  - C13 Action trigger: 51 of 1,018 records; share 0.050. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C13]]
  - C5 Comparison & decision load: 22 of 1,018 records; share 0.022. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C5]]
  - D1 Cost surprise: 14 of 1,018 records; share 0.014. [[analysis_code_prevalence|D1]]
- Source coverage for C6 (platform-artefact risk)
  - C6 appears in 4 sources overall. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]]
  - Reddit: 74 of 309; share 0.239. [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C6]]
  - YouTube: 70 of 573; share 0.122. [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C6]]
  - Google Play: 60 of 114; share 0.526. [[analysis_source_code|play|C6]]
  - App Store: 3 of 22; share 0.136. [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C6]]
- Counterfactuals for C6 (do users say they’d buy if cheaper?)
  - C6 counterfactuals: 31 of 201 price-coded records; share 0.154. [[analysis_counterfactuals|C6]]
  - D1 counterfactuals: 3 of 14; share 0.214. [[analysis_counterfactuals|D1]]
  - C5 counterfactuals: 4 of 21; share 0.190. [[analysis_counterfactuals|C5]]
- Co-occurrence that may shape causality
  - C13 Action trigger co-occurs with C6: 20 joint mentions; lift 1.929. [[analysis_cooccurrence|C13|C6]]

In users' words
- “i can't afford it” [[rec|9a31dad2f2c609b7e8b6f2f356bf722af6124d9a]]
- “Great Service but Price Are Slightly Higher than other platforms” [[rec|83f902cade59dd75d0914095fcae5638b5ab90ae]]
- “The original price is apparently 1665… maybe they have less pieces of XS and XL… and therefore have a smaller sale on them compared to other sizes. Super weird though” [[rec|521b042e655fdbbfdc6ddd575c0480be907551f7]]

Variation
- By source, C6 is present across Reddit, YouTube, Google Play, and the App Store, with shares of 0.239 (74/309), 0.122 (70/573), 0.526 (60/114), and 0.136 (3/22) respectively. [[analysis_source_code|reddit|C6]] [[analysis_source_code|youtube|C6]] [[analysis_source_code|play|C6]] [[analysis_source_code|appstore|C6]]
- Interpretation: The high share on Google Play may reflect app-store review skew noted in the method flags rather than a true platform effect.

Counter-evidence
- Rival barriers are also prominent in discussion, led by C2 at 241 of 1,018 (share 0.237), which exceeds C6’s 207 of 1,018 (share 0.203). [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]]
- C3 (154 of 1,018; share 0.151) and C7 (140 of 1,018; share 0.138) are also frequently raised. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C3]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C7]]
- Intent extinguished after saving (C12) is present at 54 of 1,018 (share 0.053), offering an alternative explanation where desire fades independently of price. [[analysis_code_prevalence|C12]]
- Interpretation: Not all price talk is framed as “would have bought if cheaper”; the counterfactual rate for C6 is limited to 31 of 201, and some records emphasize cross-platform comparison or confusion about sale mechanics rather than a definitive purchase intent.

Confidence
- Medium. C6 and C1 have reliable agreement with the human coder (kappa 0.645 for C6; 0.657 for C1). [[analysis_gold_agreement|C6]] [[analysis_gold_agreement|C1]]
- However, two validation thresholds fail at the study level, and several other codes have “not measurable” reliability, which tempers confidence. [[analysis_method_flags|gold_thresholds_failed]]

Limitations
- This corpus measures shares of discussion by people who chose to post, not user actions or conversion rates. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_funnel]]
- The relevance rubric is narrow and, on a hand-read sample, excluded material that skews toward price/value and delivery-and-trust; rankings are conditional on this filter. [[analysis_method_flags|narrow_relevance_rubric]]
- Only about 36% of the relevant corpus is Myntra-specific; platform-mechanical inferences about Myntra rest on a smaller base. [[analysis_method_flags|myntra_specific_share]]
- Source independence is limited to roughly three source types; app-store reviews are a distinct and skewed genre. [[analysis_method_flags|three_independent_source_types]]
- Segments are derived from codes; associations with undecided states are partly circular. [[analysis_method_flags|segments_derived_not_observed]]
- Some codes have small counts and are “too thin to report” more granularly (e.g., D1 at 14/1,018; C5 at 22/1,018), so fine-grained breakdowns by source or subcode are not reliable. [[analysis_code_prevalence|D1]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C5]] [[analysis_method_flags|min_n_floor]]
- Price is constrained by “no monetary incentives”; findings should be read as opportunities for transparency, anchoring, and timing, not discounting. [[analysis_method_flags|no_monetary_incentive]]

Interpretation:
- Is C6 “the single biggest barrier”? Not in this corpus: C2 is raised slightly more often. Still, C6 is a major eliminator, present across sources, with some explicit “would buy if cheaper” statements and signs that price interacts with timing (co-occurs with Action trigger C13). [[analysis_code_prevalence|C2]] [[analysis_code_prevalence|C6]] [[analysis_counterfactuals|C6]] [[analysis_cooccurrence|C13|C6]]
- What do people mean by price? The quotes reflect both affordability (“i can't afford it”) and perceived relative value versus other platforms or sizes (“Price Are Slightly Higher”; “smaller sale… compared to other sizes”), pointing to anchoring and sale mechanics as part of the price story. [[rec|9a31dad2f2c609b7e8b6f2f356bf722af6124d9a]] [[rec|83f902cade59dd75d0914095fcae5638b5ab90ae]] [[rec|521b042e655fdbbfdc6ddd575c0480be907551f7]]
